Growth & demand: During his tenure, he has been involved in the Company's business and strategic initiatives, with a focus on supporting the growth and development of its textile and related business operations.

Domestic demand held firm, particularly in urban apparel, technical textiles, and home furnishings, while export growth remained constrained by soft demand in Europe and the United States and by intensifying competition from lower-cost manufacturing bases.

Global GDP growth remained subdued, in the region of 2.7-3.0%, as elevated financing costs, softer consumption in the US and EU, and fragmented trade flows continued to weigh on capital-intensive and export-oriented sectors.

This improvement was driven by disciplined cost management, a more favourable raw-material and power-cost profile in relative terms, lower finance costs, and an improved product mix, which together lifted operating margins even on a lower revenue base.

Finance costs declined to ₹74.63 lakhs from ₹102.44 lakhs, reflecting continued balance-sheet discipline, while other income rose to ₹74.71 lakhs, aided partly by the gain on sale of property, plant and equipment.
Capex & expansion: India again distinguished itself as one of the fastest-growing major economies, supported by resilient domestic consumption, sustained government capital expenditure, and a broad-based manufacturing and services expansion.

Financial Position and Liquidity As at 31 st March 2026, the Company's total assets stood at ₹5,480.83 lakhs, compared with ₹6,003.31 lakhs a year earlier, reflecting reduction in property, plant and equipment, inventories, and trade receivables.

Balance sheet & cash: The Company generated positive cash flow from operations of ₹211.87 lakhs, enabling continued servicing of obligations and modest capital investment.
Total Equity was ₹2,601.88 lakhs and non-current borrowings stood at ₹1,257.30 lakhs.
The Company generated net cash from operating activities of ₹211.87 lakhs during the year and continued to service its financing obligations, ending the year with a modestly improved cash position.
Risks & challenges: Risks and Concerns The Company remains exposed to raw-material price volatility, foreign-exchange fluctuations on account of its export exposure, evolving global trade and tariff policies, and competitive pricing pressures.

Outlook Despite near-term headwinds arising from an uncertain global trade environment and competitive pricing pressures, the medium- to long-term outlook for the Indian textile sector remains constructive, supported by domestic demand, favourable policy measures, and global sourcing diversification.
